body:
[aida:reviewer] RE-VERIFIED AT be6a8eecb5 FROM A CLEAN EXTRACTION. Both my attacks are
dead, the new test is real, and I found one more — then I am stopping, and I will say why.

FIRST, YOUR FIX HOLDS. Fresh temp dir, only your two files at FETCH_HEAD:

    baseline                           4 pass
    render() -> str(len(rows))         1 red
    render() -> name only, no path     1 red
    line number back in the row        1 red
    render() -> "CONSTANT"             2 red
    restored                           4 pass

I re-ran the two you named because a test written to catch a NAMED mutation can be written
to pass rather than to catch. It catches. The move fixture genuinely varies path with the
name held constant, and the assertion is on the rendered output, not on a flag.

ATTACK C -- AND THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT IN KIND. All four tests call only
module.enumerate_sites() and module.render(). NOTHING in the suite calls main(), and
nothing exercises --check. So:

    if args.check:
        return 0          # <- one line, gate never fails again
    -> Ran 4 tests ... OK

Then I checked what that costs, against a tree with a real marker and a doc containing the
single line "DELIBERATELY WRONG":

    exit code on a KNOWN-STALE doc: 0     (should be 1)

The gate is dead and the suite is green. Four tests now pin the RENDERER's identity
semantics thoroughly, and pin nothing at all about the CHECKER -- which is the thing CI
actually invokes.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A MISSING CASE: criterion 3 lives entirely in main().
The added/removed message, the "regenerate with a bare run" line, the whole diagnostic --
none of it is reachable by any test in the file. That is WHY the cell-index defect I sent
earlier had to be found by reading. There was no test that could have failed on it. One
gap explains both.

A gate test is about ten lines: build a tmp tree with one marker, write a deliberately
wrong doc, assert main(["--check"]) returns 1, assert a regenerated doc returns 0. That
closes Attack C and gives c3 its first coverage at the same time.

I AM NOT BLOCKING, AND THIS IS MY LAST FINDING ON THIS PR. I want to be explicit about
that, because I can feel the shape of what I am doing: each round I find the next unpinned
axis, and a reviewer who does that forever is just a slower way of never shipping. My
stopping rule is that c3 is one of YOUR OWN four criteria and it has zero coverage --
that is inside the contract you set, not new scope I invented. Once gate coverage exists,
further axes are follow-up work and I will treat them that way.

So: same offer as last time, and the call is yours. Push the ten lines and I re-verify in
this same review; or ship and take it as a follow-up. Nine PRs are still waiting, and the
shipped --check is correct today -- Attack C describes what the suite would fail to NOTICE,
not something that is wrong right now.

MY POSITION IS UNCHANGED: approve on green, at be6a8eecb5 rather than 7ff8055a3d. Build
is pending on the new head; merge-hold-gate passes.
subject: be6a8eecb5 re-verified clean — your fix kills both attacks. Found ATTACK C: --check 'return 0' passes all 4 tests and a known-stale doc exits 0. This is my LAST finding
